In early 2025 Unilever’s new CEO, Fernando Fernandez, highlighted the necessity of making brands more relevant and participatory by leveraging the reach and authenticity of creators and social communities. He shifted 50% of his media budget to social and creators - that’s $5 BILLION US DOLLARS annually."
""
"Unilever’s creator and social strategy for next year’s World Cup is the exact game plan brands should be playing if they want to deliver business results."
""
"Here’s my take on why it matters:"
""
"1.⁠ ⁠Scale + relevance doesn't come from broadcast alone"
"Unilever plans “to dispatch an army of creators across North America” at the World Cup. That means local stories, platform native content and creators who already connect in niche markets. This is exactly how to invest in and deliver content that converts."
""
"2.⁠ ⁠Sponsorship + creator ecosystem = multiplier"
"Sponsorship gives you access to the moment, but it’s social media that activates it. A rights deal alone won’t drive cultural impact. The real ROI comes when socially-driven distribution translates that sponsorship into everyday conversations across the platforms where people are spending their time."
""
"3.⁠ ⁠Measurable outcomes over mere exposure"
"The big shift isn’t just more creators. It’s shifting budget and measurement from TV/display to social impact and creators, with performance measurement built in. It’s investing in the moment where attention actually lives. For travel, tourism or any brand chasing an event moment, you need to be thinking about engagement and conversation, not just reach, and that’s where creators come in."
""
"We saw this play out with Coca-Cola’s Paris 2024 Olympic creator strategy where they sent 10,000 creators behind the scenes. The result? Their content outperformed traditional coverage across multiple platforms and drove a stronger audience connection, with 49% of consumers surveyed choosing Coca-Cola as the sponsor most associated with the Olympics."
""
"The World Cup is one of the biggest moments in sport, and investing in creators for that moment is what will build community and cultural momentum long after the final whistle."
""
"Looking forward to seeing how this strategy rolls out Unilever Fernando Fernandez Esi Eggleston Bracey Ryu Yokoi Emily Heath 👏

posts.full_text:
If you were measuring tourism success the traditional way, Barcelona would be unstoppable."
""
"The traditional way:"
"→ Are we attracting more visitors?"
"→ Can we get them to stay longer?"
"→ Can we encourage them to spend more?"
""
"In 2024, Barcelona did just that, hosting over 26 million visitors that year alone. That’s more than x15 its population. "
""
"Sounds great, but in reality:"
"→ Residents are being forced out of their homes due to rising real estate prices"
"→ There have been multiple protests from residents against tourism in Barcelona "
"→ Residents claim that Barcelona's traditional identity and character have been eroded in favour of tourism  "
""
"That’s what the ‘traditional’ model has led to. And that’s why the definition of tourism success is being rewritten by some tourism boards."
""
"Instead of asking ‘How do we get more people?’ they’re asking ‘How do we manage more people?’. "
""
"Here are some of the effective ways I’ve seen destinations adapting: "
""
"1.⁠ ⁠Seasonality Balance"
"Reducing pressure during peak months is now a strategic goal for overcrowded destinations. Instead of pushing high-season numbers further, tourism boards are investing in campaigns that shift interest into shoulder and off-peak periods, protecting both residents and the destination’s long-term appeal."
""
"2.⁠ ⁠Local Impact & Community Benefit"
"Tourism boards are tracking how visitor spending supports local businesses, creates jobs, and helps the wider local economies. Some destinations, like Spain and Italy, even use tourism impact scores or community satisfaction surveys to quantify this."
""
"3.⁠ ⁠Brand Perception & Sentiment"
"Destination marketing is also about identity. Tourism boards are monitoring global search data, social sentiment, and reputation studies to understand how people feel about their country. This means KPIs are made from tourism numbers mixed with satisfaction."
""
"Tourism success today is just as much about perception and balance as it is about growth. That's how the modern tourism board measures success."
""
"I’ve posted more about the topic of over-tourism this year as I believe social media and video content can have a positive impact. I want to learn what’s working, what areas could do with help and who’s leading initiatives to address this (not just criticising on LinkedIn!), so please let me know any examples you know of and reach out if you have ideas to share 😁🙏
posts.hook: If you were measuring tourism success the traditional way, Barcelona would be unstoppable."

The 2006 Men’s Football World Cup was powered by print and TV."
""
"The 2026 Men’s Football World Cup will be powered by creators and social."
""
"Just 20 years between the events, and global sports travel has changed entirely."
""
"Back then:"
"→ Flights were booked through travel agents."
"→ Hotels were filled through offline wholesalers."
"→ Marketing relied on TV and print."
"→ Global reach depended on who had the best broadcast slot."
""
"Fast forward twenty years, and everything about how we see and experience major sporting events has changed."
""
"→ Digital Distribution"
"In 2006, most fans booked their trips through agents or call centres. In 2026, over 80% of travellers will book online or via mobile, with airline, hotel, and destination data syncing in real time. The journey from ticket to take-off is now entirely digital."
""
"→ The Creator & Content Economy"
"Back then, travel content creators didn’t even exist. In 2026, they will be the broadcast network, shaping where fans stay, what they experience, and how the world sees the host nation."
""
"→ Experience Over Accommodation"
"Years ago, fans typically prioritised proximity to the stadium, but now we're seeing fans build complete destination itineraries around huge cultural events. They want to experience the local food, culture, and sights and they’re inspired by what they can find on social media when they’re planning."
""
"Tourism Exchange USA found that 77% of travellers say they now prioritise the experience of the trip over the cost and in a world where Expedia estimates over three quarters of travellers have used social media in the planning process… You can bet those experiences have been watched as videos long before they are booked."
""
"In this new era of global travel and live tourism, experience is the product and social is the medium.

"Visit Sweden just launched one of the smartest tourism campaigns of the year- it’s called The Swedish Prescription and it prescribes the destination, instead of selling it."

I’ve experienced this first hand as every year I go to an amazing conference in Stockholm, Brilliant Minds Foundation run by some close friends Shakil Khan and Annastasia Seebohm Giacomini, that embodies all the values of Swedishness and the benefits of life in the country."
""
"This kind of tourism marketing is becoming more prevalent - and more effective, as destinations move away from big, traditional brand advertising campaigns and lean more into the lifestyle decisions of potential travellers."
""
"This is the approach more destinations need to adopt, as more travellers look for the depth behind every destination."
""
"Congratulations on a great idea, Nils Persson and Susanne Andersson!

One of the most pivotal moments for Beautiful Destinations was thanks to my brother."
""
"I’m not sure Beautiful Destinations would exist today if this moment hadn’t happened…"
""
"In the early days, we didn't make our own content."
""
"We focused on finding talented photographers and videographers (long before they were called creators) and sharing their work on our channels."
""
"It was working incredibly well, but we felt something was missing. Then my brother made a suggestion and we decided to completely change the business."
""
"He suggested we create the content ourselves. He decided to pick up a camera for the first time aged 28 and the rest is history. "
""
"In hindsight, it sounds obvious but over a decade ago, it sounded crazy. Traditional production companies were still running everything, they had huge crews, huge budgets and long timelines to play with. "
""
"We were in New York, surrounded by Madison Avenue agencies with entire floors of directors, producers, creative directors and designers who took pleasure in telling us they were going to crush us."
""
"But we decided to do it anyway."
""
"We had no idea, and taught ourselves everything. How to shoot, how to edit, how to tell stories for the new platforms and most importantly, how to identify the next generation of creative talent."
""
"It was completely different from how the big players operated, but that decision gave us something they didn’t have: the ability to scale creativity from the inside out and to really know how to market travel."
""
"Fast-forward 10 years and that decision turned out to be the backbone of our business. Thankfully the market agreed as the world is moving away from big productions and towards the speed, authenticity and creativity of individual creators. "
""
"We took the risk, backed ourselves and it paid off."
""
"He’s still my little brother though so don’t tell him I said this 😉
posts.hook: One of the most pivotal moments for Beautiful Destinations was thanks to my brother."

posts.full_text:
When your flight price jumps overnight, it’s not random."
""
"I’ve been thinking about the systems that sit behind the travel industry. The ones that are second nature to those of us who work in it, but are almost invisible to the everyday traveller."
""
"Behind every seat price is a data model balancing demand, competition, and even your browsing behaviour."
""
"So, for those who are interested, or for those who have ever wondered."
""
"Here’s how airline pricing actually works:"
""
"1.⁠ ⁠Base Fare (typically 40-60%)"
"This covers the core cost of operating a flight: aircraft fuel, crew, airport slots, maintenance, and insurance. These are the costs that airlines generally have the least control over. Fuel prices rise with global events, airport slots vary by place, and maintenance standards are non-negotiable."
""
"2.⁠ ⁠Dynamic Pricing"
"Modern airlines use real-time algorithms to analyse demand, route popularity, seasonality, competitor pricing, and even search volume. That’s why you might see a fare jump from £220 to £295 in a matter of hours, it’s the system responding to supply and demand."
""
"3.⁠ ⁠Ancillary Revenue (typically 10-20%)"
"Seat selection, baggage, Wi-Fi, meals, upgrades, these extras often make the biggest difference to an airline’s bottom line. For low-cost airlines, ancillary sales can be more profitable than the base ticket itself."
""
"4.⁠ ⁠Distribution Fees (10-15%)"
"When you book through online travel agents or third-party platforms, a percentage of your fare goes to the distribution systems and partners that connect you to the airline, like Expedia."
""
"5.⁠ ⁠Taxes & Surcharges (15-25%)"
"Airport fees, fuel surcharges, and government taxes can make up nearly a quarter of your final ticket price. These are costs the airline takes but doesn’t necessarily control."
""
"For most travellers, all of this is invisible."
""
"But understanding how these systems work gives a different appreciation for the complexity of airlines and the process it takes to fly the 10-12 million travellers around the world every day."
""
"What looks like a simple ticket price is actually the outcome of thousands of variables working in real time and that's how airline pricing really works."
""

posts.full_text:
Every major sporting event is a tourism campaign in disguise…"
""
"From the World Cup to the Olympics to Formula 1, these events are real-time opportunities to invest in long-term transformation. Rafat Ali Skift often calls these events ‘Live Tourism,’ and it’s a huge opportunity in travel."
""
"Billions go into infrastructure, media, and global positioning that last many years beyond the sports events."
""
"Here’s how countries get sports tourism right 👇"
""
"1. Infrastructure before experience"
""
"Mega-events accelerate the development of airports, hotels, and transport networks that reshape travel access for decades. What’s built for a few weeks of competition becomes the foundation for long-term connectivity. For the Qatar World Cup in 2022, the country invested $200 billion, positioning Doha as a long-term tourism hub. Dubai did the same with Expo 2020. The event welcomed over 24 million visitors and hosted 192 countries, and since then, it has been transformed into Expo City Dubai, a mixed-use development. "
""
"2. Content as legacy"
""
"Broadcast coverage, creator partnerships, and digital storytelling position destinations favourably, even if they're not the host country. Long after the closing ceremony, that storytelling content keeps audiences engaged, as memes and iconic moments make viral videos (anyone else still get the Dutch football fans “left right” jumping in unison videos around Germany from Euro 2024?!)"
""
"3. Local economies rebranded"
""
"Cities use these events to shift perception, from industrial to cultural. Hosting creates a narrative that redefines national identity through the lens of travel. Just look at the 2026 World Cup, it's set to be a multi-city format that distributes benefits and exposure across a continent, blending the best of American, Mexican and Canadian culture. Name a tourism campaign that could do that on its own?"
""
"4. The afterglow effect"
""
"For many, the real ROI comes after the event. When awareness turns into aspiration, and aspiration turns into a boost in tourism numbers. It can be months, it can be years, it can even be decades but the impact is there, as are the dollars."
""
"Sport can be the catalyst to put your destination in the spotlight globally."
""
"Thanks to everyone who fed back on my ‘How It Works’ series, exploring the mechanics behind the global travel industry. I had so many great comments, I'll continue sharing the behind-the-scenes. Let me know what you want to know next in the comments.
posts.hook: Every major sporting event is a tourism campaign in disguise…"

""

posts.full_text:
The World Cup is coming next year, and as much of a fan as I am of the sport… I’m as big a fan of looking at its marketing. "
""
"It’s a fascinating exercise to chart the differences in how each World Cup markets itself, as in the four years between each competition, so much changes in how to talk to consumers."
""
"Here’s what I mean…."
""
"Listed here is every single partner of the World Cup from 1982 - 2022."
""
"For decades, global events like the World Cup and the Olympics have followed the same playbook:"
""
"10 to 15 massive global sponsors tied into broadcast rights and TV-first deals."
""
"The official beverage title has been Coca-Cola every year since 1974, and we’ve seen the same names on the sponsorsheets for years - Budweiser, Adidas, and Canon, to name a few."
""
"The model is still primarily built for a world where attention lives on television, but that doesn't represent the world we live in anymore."
""
"The next generation of fans experience the game through creators, memes, and short-form content on social, as well as live coverage."
""
"So the question I want to explore is:"
"How will the next wave of global sponsors stay relevant when the audience isn’t watching TV?"
""
"This is where I think the biggest opportunity lies - rethinking what sponsorship looks like in a social-first world."
""
"→ How can tourism boards build activations that live natively on TikTok, Reels or WhatsApp instead of halftime ads?"
"→ How can brands partner with creators who capture the emotion of the game rather than putting their logo alongside 100s of others on the pitch?"
"→ How can destinations around the world use the global spotlight to tell their story to millions who might never even see the TV broadcast?"
""
"Big broadcast advertising is expensive and I'd argue, increasingly inefficient."
""
"The same investment, redirected into digital and social experiences, could reach more people, in more meaningful ways, with more measurable impact."
""
"Does anyone have examples they like that I could learn from?
posts.hook: The World Cup is coming next year, and as much of a fan as I am of the sport… I’m as big a fan of looking at its marketing. "

The biggest barrier for travel marketing right now?"
""
"High-quality video at scale."

"The scalability of video has long been a problem for most travel brands. Photography has always been easier, faster, and cheaper to produce, but AI is closing that gap fast."
""
"Just a few weeks ago, OpenAI released Sora 2, which can now generate dialogue, background ambience, and sound effects alongside visuals. It is insanely powerful, and I’m excited about what it brings to our business and industry. "
""
"Some thoughts:"
""
"→ Destinations and hotels can now produce video-first campaigns at scale, without the same production overhead & complexity"
""
"→ High-quality creator content becomes more valuable, as high-quality inputs to AI, generate the highest quality outputs"
""
"→ Budgets stretch further, and pipelines move faster."
""
"AI is an important tool for the future of our industry. I’m excited about what it can bring to the content creation process, and at BD, we’ve jumped in fully. We’re working on some technology and testing it with a handful of clients, which I think will be impactful for our business and the industry."
""
"Underpinning it all, however, is high-quality source footage. We believe that world-class creative inputs (from creators) lead to world-class AI-supported outputs and that the combination of real people, real content and technology is where the magic lies.
posts.hook: The biggest barrier for travel marketing right now?"

posts.full_text:
For those of us working in travel, it’s easy to forget how much knowledge we take for granted."
""
"Most travelers will never see how their hotel spend is actually split, the commissions, fees, and taxes that sit behind the booking process. "
""
"Throughout my career in travel, I’ve always tried to pass on my learnings as much as possible to those new to the industry, and that’s what I hope to do with my LinkedIn posts."
""
"So, when someone pays $300 for a night’s stay, where does that money really go? Broadly speaking,"
""
"→ Base Room Cost (typically 45-60%)"
"The biggest share covers operations (staff wages, housekeeping, maintenance, food & beverage, and utilities)"
""
"→ OTA Commissions (typically 15-25%)"
"If the guest books through an online travel agency, a significant portion goes straight to distribution costs. It’s the price hotels pay for visibility, reach, data, marketing, etc.."
""
"→ Brand + Franchise Fees (typically 5-10%)"
"Chain properties contribute back to their parent brand for loyalty programs, marketing, and technology systems. This can vary a lot by brand."
""
"→ Taxes + Tourism Levies (typically 10-20%)"
"Destination taxes fund infrastructure and tourism boards, but often go unseen by travelers."
""
"→ Growth + Reinvestment (typically 5%)"
"A small fraction supports property upgrades, sustainability initiatives, and staff training. Again this can vary a lot by brand."
""
"After everything, that $300 booking might leave the hotel with closer to $150-$180 in gross operating profit. The true take-home profit is even lower than this."
""
"And it raises an interesting question - if more travelers understood the mechanics behind their journeys, would they value the experience differently?"
""
"When people see what really goes into a stay, from the staff behind the scenes to the systems that keep the industry running, travel becomes more than a transaction."
""
"For my non-hospitality friends- is this helpful or interesting? I’m thinking of a “how this works” series to share more about how our industry brings value to people and would love feedback or ideas. Thanks!"
""
"📸 From our Summer holidays in Greece 🇬🇷 🌊
posts.hook: For those of us working in travel, it’s easy to forget how much knowledge we take for granted."

"The best tourism ideas have always been simple, emotional, and globally shareable. I think the foundations that worked in 2009 still apply today, and with the power of social media and content creators, you can bring viral, impactful ideas to life easily."

"

It’s estimated that over 5 million road trips happen every year on Route 66."

"Route 66 stretches 2,400 miles across eight U.S. states, from Chicago to Santa Monica, and in 2026, it will celebrate its 100th anniversary."
""
"That’s a marketing opportunity for the taking:"
"→ 2.3M Instagram posts are already tagged #Route66 without coordinated campaigns."
""
"→ Travelers spend $1,500–$2,000 per trip, fueling the thousands of small towns built around the route."
""
"→ The last major study estimated $132M in direct annual spend, and communities in a new study (Route 66, Revisited) say visitor growth is already building as the centenary approaches."
""
"The centenary should create an attention spike. I think there is an opportunity for travel brands to turn that global fascination into campaigns that not only drive bookings, but channel economic impact back into the communities that keep Route 66 alive."
""
"Leveraging high-quality video content to bring to life all the amazing things that happen on the route, the right strategy should inspire people to do the drive now. It’s been on my bucket list for ages."
""
"Nearly a century later, Route 66 is proof that heritage and storytelling can be more powerful than budget. The centenary will test which brands know how to use storytelling to their advantage."
""
"I’m looking forward to seeing the campaigns for the 100th anniversary… who knows, maybe Beautiful Destinations will be part of it 😉😎

posts.full_text:
The next era of hotel branding is about individuality at scale."
""
"Yesterday, Hilton announced Outset Collection, a lifestyle brand targeting independent hotels. With more than 60 properties already in development, it joins a growing wave of “soft brands” reshaping hospitality."
""
"Chris Silcock, President of Global Brands and Commercial Services at Hilton, said this launch is the result of traveler's wanting more unique, one-of-a-kind hotels and experiences."
""
"For years, global chains like Hilton, Marriott, and Hyatt focused on consistency - the idea that a traveler could wake up in any city in the world and know exactly what to expect."
""
"That model built trust and added a sense of familiarity, but it also made many hotels lack individuality."
""
"Now, the industry is shifting."
""
"Travelers want individuality, and soft brands let major groups deliver both."
""
"They let global groups offer individuality with infrastructure through distinct storytelling, design, and community, backed by the reliability of a bigger chain."
""
"IHG claims that conversions (independent hotels converting to its brands) made up about 60% of global openings in Q1 2025, showing how soft brands and conversion-friendly strategies are playing a big role in current hotel growth."
""
"The challenge for every major hotel group now is how to scale individuality whilst keeping familiarity and consistency."
""
"I would love to hear more opinions on this shift from my friends and connections in the hotel industry 🙏
posts.hook: The next era of hotel branding is about individuality at scale."

Since its debut in 2008, the Singapore Grand Prix has attracted over 550,000 international visitors and generated around $2 billion in incremental tourism spend."
""
"The data shows visitors are staying beyond the race to experience Singapore’s food, nightlife, and culture."

"Data from Singapore Tourism Board found that during race week, visitors stay almost twice as long as the average tourist, around 7 nights compared to the average 3 or 4, boosting the impact across hotels, restaurants, and cultural attractions."
""
"It’s a clear example of the ripple effect live events can have on destinations:"
" → Hotels report higher occupancy and premium room rates"
"→ Shopping, dining and entertainment categories all see huge growth"
"→ The destination has millions watching worldwide"
""
"Singapore’s tourism sector is on the rise, with international arrivals projected to reach nearly 16 million in 2025, exceeding pre-pandemic levels."
""
"And, the Formula One race pushes growth even further. Visa data from 2024 showed the race week alone drove a 20% surge in inbound travel and a 30% increase in tourist spending in Singapore."
""
"With a contract to host F1 until 2028, the country has created a benchmark for how destinations can use live events to drive growth, extend stays, and strengthen its positioning worldwide."
""
"The stats for this year are looking promising, looking forward to seeing how it plays out this weekend - great work Melissa Ow, Kenneth Lim and the team at Singapore Tourism Board 😎"
""

For decades, points defined loyalty in travel."
""
"But today, acquisition costs are rising, travellers are harder to win back, and loyalty has to mean more than transactions. Points are transactional. Experiences are emotional."
""
"The most forward-thinking leaders are proving that the future of loyalty is about experiences, emotions and community."
""
"But who is driving this evolution? Here are five leaders who are leading the way:"
""
"Brad Anderson, Hilton → Scaling Hilton Honours to 226M+ members worldwide, showing how global loyalty needs both breadth and depth."
""
"Peggy Roe, Marriott International → Turning loyalty into live experiences with initiatives like “Member’s Day,” moving beyond perks to connection."
""
"Scott Long, American Airlines → Evolving the first-ever frequent flyer program into a major revenue driver through strategic partnerships."
""
"Cecilie Nybø Carlsen, Norwegian → Making loyalty transparent by treating CashPoints like currency (1 point = 1 Krone)."
""
"Andrew Harrison-Chinn, Dragonpass → Expanding loyalty into lifestyle, proving that benefits shouldn’t stop at flights and hotels."
""
"The future of loyalty in travel will be built on experiences that matter, communities that last, and emotional connections that keep travelers coming back long after the points are spent."
""
"Thank you to all of these leaders paving the way 🙏
posts.hook: For decades, points defined loyalty in travel."

Can you imagine a road trip where you never know where you’re going next? "
""
"That’s exactly what the Faroe Islands are offering."
""
"Their new initiative gives visitors self-navigating itineraries where Google Maps reveals one stop at a time, only after you’ve completed the last leg of the journey."
""
"On the surface, it’s a clever way to inject spontaneity. But it's actually a smart response to one of the industry’s biggest challenges: overtourism."
""
"By controlling the flow of visitors in real time, the Faroes can:"
"→ Redistribute travellers away from crowded hotspots"
"→ Encourage exploration of lesser-known villages and landscapes"
"→ Reduce the strain on fragile ecosystems and communities"
""
"It’s a subtle but powerful example of how design and technology can solve a systemic issue."
""
"Because overtourism will only be fixed by smarter distribution and better storytelling."
""
"We’ve already seen alternative approaches like Copenhagen’s CopenPay by Wonderful Copenhagen, which rewards contribution over consumption, free kayaks for picking up rubbish or lunch for tending a community garden."
""
"The Faroes’ “as-you-go itineraries” point to another model: using infrastructure and tech to spread visitors out and help them discover beyond the obvious."
""
"Both examples share the same idea that travel becomes more meaningful when it benefits both the visitor and the destination. "
""
"Great work Guðrið Højgaard, Susanna Sørensen and the Visit Faroe Islands team!
posts.hook: Can you imagine a road trip where you never know where you’re going next? "

Every year, Skift Global Forum sets the tone for where travel is heading."
""
"My good friends at Skift, Rafat Ali, Jason Clampet, Sean O'Neill and team always put on a brilliant event, and I’ve thoroughly enjoyed hearing the insights from the leaders this year."
""
"Three themes stood out to me that all travel brands should be paying attention to now:"
""
"1. The disruption opportunity"
"Osamah Alnuaiser, SVP at Riyadh Air | طيران الرياض, shared how the airline is entering the market with a bold ambition to fix the gaps legacy airlines have left open, with a huge focus on mobile discovery and booking. No matter how many years you have in the game, it’s a reminder that disruption always comes from spotting unmet traveler expectations. Do more of that and you’re winning. "
""
"2. Retention vs. acquisition"
"Audrey Hendley, President of American Express Travel, spoke about how they are aiming to build loyalty with numerous benefits, and how the company is balancing between trust and innovation after 175 years in business. Rising acquisition costs and fragmented booking journeys mean brands can’t just rely on chasing new customers, they have to look inwards, and that's what Amex are doing."
""
"3. Growth is moving east"
"Elie W. Maalouf, CEO of IHG Hotels & Resorts, highlighted the brand’s expansion in Japan, where they plan to double their footprint. Dubai, Japan, and wider Asia are fast becoming the hub for innovation and travel growth. It’s one of the key reasons I moved to this side of the world, the pace of growth here is world-class, and it’s shaping the future of our industry."
""
"Sadly, I couldn’t make it to New York this year but love the work Skift does and am a daily reader and supporter :)
posts.hook: Every year, Skift Global Forum sets the tone for where travel is heading."

Marriott has just hosted its first “Member’s Day”… Could it signal the future of loyalty in hospitality?"
""
"Repeat customers are more valuable now than they’ve ever been. And acquiring a new one is harder than ever."
""
"Between 2022 and 2025, Adobe found the cost to acquire new customers in travel and hospitality rose by around 35%, while customer lifetime value grew around 4.5%."
""
"Points and perks aren’t enough anymore."
""
"So how do hotels like Marriott stay close to the customer?"
""
"→ Guests tested new products, previewed rooms, and shared unfiltered feedback"
"→ Chief Customer Officer Peggy Roe turned the event into a live focus group"
"→ Nearly all of Marriott’s C-suite showed up"
""
"This is a signal of just how critical direct customer relationships have become."
""
"Marriott's CEO Anthony Capuano gets it. He's transforming Bonvoy from a 'transactional system' into an emotional one, learning directly from loyal customers why they keep spending with Marriott."
""
"In a market where discovery is happening on social, bookings are shifting from search to AI tools, loyalty can no longer equate to just a loyalty scheme."
""
"Marriott International’s approach to loyalty could be the way hotels capture changing consumer behaviour for long lasting, profitable relationships.

posts.full_text:
Visitors to Las Vegas have dropped by 12% in the past year but I think a socially driven content strategy could help change that trajectory…"
""
"High prices, reduced consumer spending and a shift towards wealthier travellers have all played a part. In response, the city launched its first brand campaign since 2018, “Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas.”"
""
"It’s a brilliant piece of advertising, but imagine pairing it with the reach and cultural influence of organic social content and creators."
""
"Firstly, great social content finds its audience - the algorithms will push a user content which is relevant for them. Branded content is always flagged, so instead of organic discovery, you need to pay to push it."
""
"Paid advertising is critically important, but campaigns can be so much more impactful when combined with dedicated social content that is tailored per platform and organically finds its audience."
""
"Second, creators have influence by showing destinations differently to traditional marketers. The best ones inspire & educate so their audiences see something they wouldn’t in a traditional ad."
""
"They’ve built a personal, trusted relationship with those that follow them because of this. It’s why we’re so bullish on them."
""
"As with my point above, it’s the combination that is the solution and we’re seeing this work on a global scale as more destinations do both:"
""
"→ ‘Tourism New Zealand’s '100% Pure' campaign paired traditional advertising with creator partnerships that showcased Kiwi experiences. The combination drove record levels of engagement for the country."
""
"→ Japan’s “Come to Japan” campaign ran traditional TV and media alongside a social-first campaign with virtual YouTuber Kizuna Ai, bringing in a whole new Gen Z audience on YouTube too."
""
"There was a huge opportunity when Ryan Trahan visited Las Vegas as part of his ’50 States in 50 Days’ series, his Vegas episode reached 5.7M viewers organically. If you look at the comments on the post I made about him last month, they were overwhelmingly positive."
""
"A strategy that combines traditional advertising with social first content & creator-led storytelling could help Vegas (and any other destination) discover with new audiences and reverse the decline."
""
"Congratulations on the campaign Kate (Vuturo) Wik, Nikki Rosetti, Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority - LVCVA, excited to see how it evolves 😎
posts.hook: Visitors to Las Vegas have dropped by 12% in the past year but I think a socially driven content strategy could help change that trajectory…"

posts.full_text:
For years, we’ve helped global travel brands cut through on one of the noisiest platforms in the world. "
""
"So here's the YouTube playbook we’re now applying to grow Beautiful Destinations' own channel:"
""
"1. Signature Formats"
"Creators are building formats that audiences can come back to again and again. BD launched BD Originals. Ryan Trahan recently blew up with his 50 States in 50 Days."
""
"2. Obsess over analytics"
"YouTube is the only platform that gives you second-by-second drop-off data. That means you can identify exactly where viewers lose interest and build tighter, more engaging stories. Every edit, cut, and thumbnail we produce is guided by this data."
""
"3. Organise channels like seasons of a TV Show"
"BD structures channels like a season of television. Each episode connects to a bigger narrative arc, designed to build long-term loyalty, not just short-term clicks."
""
"4. Treat thumbnails, titles and descriptions as its own product"
"Most success on YouTube comes before someone even clicks play. We treat thumbnails and titles as their own creative product - they shouldn’t be an afterthought. Test and refine."
""
"Even by the time you’ve finished reading this post, there will be 2,500 videos uploaded to YouTube."
""
"That’s over 2.6 million per day, according to Photutorial. "
""
"With that level of output, it’s so hard to stand out, but it’s something our team have been able to consistently prove they can do with travel storytelling. "
""
"For travel brands, YouTube is an opportunity to build owned IP, reach global audiences, and create stories that last."
""
"Here’s one of our recent “Let’s Go” episodes in Morocco.
posts.hook: For years, we’ve helped global travel brands cut through on one of the noisiest platforms in the world. "

What if you gave your team extra holiday days… for not flying to their holiday?"
""
"It sounds unconventional, but it’s already happening."
""
"Skift Research predicts a 24% rise in the number of trips people will take in 2025 compared to 2024. To manage the climate impact, some companies are now offering extra holiday days to employees who skip flights and choose lower-carbon travel instead."
""
"For destinations, this shift can be hugely positive:"
""
"Infrastructure → slower, longer stays reduce strain on crowded cities."
"Communities → travellers spend more locally, creating higher-value tourism."
"Travelers → the experience feels deeper, more sustainable, and ultimately more rewarding."
""
"This is a glimpse of what the future of travel incentives could look like: businesses, governments, and destinations aligning rewards to make travel better, not just faster."
""
"Travel brands should take note: the companies pioneering these incentive programs are essentially creating a new category of conscious travelers -  people with time, budget, and environmental values aligned."
""
"This demographic will drive significant demand for overland experiences, train routes, and sustainable accommodation."
""
"Would you give your team extra time off if it meant they travelled slower?
posts.hook: What if you gave your team extra holiday days… for not flying to their holiday?"

"Dennis reports that some of the industry’s fastest growth is now coming from these partnerships:"
""
"•⁠ ⁠Expedia's B2B segment surged 17% last quarter, while its consumer business grew by just 1%"
"•⁠ ⁠Booking is consolidating teams into a single global B2B unit"
"•⁠ ⁠Hopper has pivoted so completely into B2B that its consumer presence outside North America has almost vanished"

""
"At Beautiful Destinations, our Expedia Group partnership (and our Chase Travel partnership) puts us right in the middle of this shift, creating content that works across their entire B2B ecosystem - creating shoppable, data-led campaigns that combine our content & storytelling with Expedia’s global scale and distribution."
""
"Alfonso Paredes, President of Expedia’s B2B unit, is the man leading Expedia's efforts and understands how big and exciting an opportunity B2B is."
""
"The amount of change we’re seeing in the consumer travel journey this year alone is staggering. From Instagram & TikTok in social media or OpenAI & Perplexity in large language models, how a traveler ends up booking with you is more complex than it’s ever been - especially when they might now come through a bank portal or even your favourite sports teams website if the big OTAs keep growing through B2B.

"The Beautiful Destinations Academy partnered with Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism to change that, and it points to a bigger shift happening in the industry."

In 2024, Visit Oslo released a campaign that went viral with nearly 20 million views."

"The message? “Don’t come here.”"
""
"On the surface, it looked like reverse psychology. But the brilliance of the campaign was that it tapped into our fatigue with glossy, generic tourism ads that deliver a safe, predictable sea of sameness.."

"I see so many tourist boards around the world make the same mistake right now: still investing all their budgets into spotlighting only the popular landmarks and tourist traps, creating content that makes their destination indistinguishable from another."
""
"Visit Oslo did the opposite. They connected back to an idea blogger Elena Paschinger created years ago: “life-seeing”  instead of “sightseeing”. Enjoying travel for what it should be - real cultural experiences that make your life richer and connect you with a place that is different to your home."
""
"This is the kind of shift we need to see more of in travel marketing."
""
"Authenticity over aspiration."
"Depth over gloss."
"Destinations that give people a taste of the real experience, not just a curated version."
""
"As consumer behaviour evolves, the destinations that will win are the ones brave enough to go against convention, just like Thea Gunnes and the VisitOSLO team have done here.

"We moved away from the role of traditional creative directors at Beautiful Destinations and instead backed creative thinkers, who also knew how to shoot and make things happen on a production."

posts.full_text:
When we talk about overtourism, it’s easy to assume that major cultural events are a key driver."
""
"But often, they’re only a small part of the problem."
""
"This year’s 82nd Venice Film Festival will sell around 36,000 public tickets, a comparatively small number against the city’s 20–30 million annual visitors."
""
"Italian tourism spending is set to exceed 60 billion euros in 2025, and major cultural events, like the Venice Film Festival and the Carnival of Venice, are part of the key cultural make-up."
""
"But there’s a challenge: Venice is one of the world’s most delicate destinations when it comes to overtourism outside of cultural events like this."
""
"The question isn’t whether events like this should happen, but how can the city be managed sustainably the rest of the year round?"
""
"We’ve seen other countries manage tourists in the most innovative of ways:"
""
"•⁠ ⁠Department of Tourism - Bhutan makes sure tourism funds conservation through a Sustainable Development Fee of $100 per adult per night for most visitors, turning every visit into a direct investment in the country."
"•⁠ ⁠CopenPay by Wonderful Copenhagen rewards contribution over consumption, giving tourists free lunches or activities when they give back to the city through sustainable actions."
"•⁠ ⁠Vicki Miller at VisitScotland is encouraging content creation to highlight lesser-known areas, deliberately reducing promotion of already overcrowded hotspots."
""
"For Venice, a hybrid approach could be powerful:"
""
"•⁠ ⁠Campaigns that spotlight the lesser-known areas close to the city, using content to redirect attention away from the same crowded landmarks."
"•⁠ ⁠Pairing that with infrastructure changes like caps on cruise ships and dynamic pricing for day-visits. Day-trippers contribute comparatively little to the local economy compared to overnight visitors, yet massively add to congestion."
""
"Venice has already introduced a day-trip tax to begin addressing this imbalance, but scaling these kinds of measures will be key for tourism all year round."
""
"The cities that don’t have to sacrifice the essence of their culture but can work towards finding a balance will define the future of tourism.
posts.hook: When we talk about overtourism, it’s easy to assume that major cultural events are a key driver."

After more than a decade of working with travel brands around the world, one thing still surprises me:"
""
"The amount that is still relying on traditional models of marketing."
""
"So many are still using singular big-budget moments with a short shelf life and out-of-touch campaigns with celebrities."
""
"It’s fascinating to watch, and it almost feels like the industry is split into two:"
""
"1. People who understand the value of always on content and social."
"They see constant content creation as long-term brand & business drivers, not just short campaign assets. They build integrated strategies where creator content powers awareness, performance marketing, and booking"
""
"2. People fighting against the changes in the industry."
"They’re still investing the bulk of their budgets into a single high-gloss campaign, hoping it will deliver the same impact it would’ve had a decade ago, even as audiences spend more of their time, attention, and money in digital spaces."
""
"It’s clear that the travel brands and tourism boards sitting in camp one are winning."
""
"Take Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism, for example. They are building a hub of certified travel content creators and creative entrepreneurs, so they can tap into professionally trained talent at scale."
""
"Beautiful Destinations has recently worked with them on Beautiful Destinations Academy, an industry-first program that equips aspiring creators with the skills, tools, and commercial mindset to produce world-class travel content."
""
"So why do so many still cling to the traditional model?"
""
"Because it feels safe. It’s the way things have always been done. The problem is, audience behaviour has already moved on, and your marketing strategy needs to follow."
""
"The future lies with investing in creator ecosystems, building long-term partnerships, and thinking beyond the one-off moment."
""
"📸 My wife, Pia, and I, in our favourite place we now call home 🇦🇪

"They're seeing whatever information AI tools can easily summarize. "
""
"This creates a massive blind spot for travel marketers. Your brand might dominate social media, but if your content isn't structured for AI consumption, you're invisible in the fastest-growing discovery channel."
""
"That means every part of your travel experience needs to be AI-readable, AI-relevant, and AI-summarized:"
""
"•⁠ ⁠Your brand voice needs to show up clearly in AI answers"
"•⁠ ⁠Your experiences need to be described with clarity"
"•⁠ ⁠Your imagery needs metadata that AI tools can scan"
""
"This has been a shift coming for quite some time."
""
"Over a year ago, the team at Beautiful Destinations noticed this, and it contributed to our intentional shift from inspirational content to educational content that teaches the audience and answers real questions."
""
"Educational content is what consumers remember and what AI surfaces first. Lean into that!

People are no longer traveling to tick off their bucket list…"
""
"Travel is currently seeing a rise in experiences that prioritize stillness, movement, and mental clarity over adrenaline or bucket-list ticking."
""
"By the end of 2025, Wellness tourism is projected to reach $1.3 trillion, according to the Global Wellness Institute."
""
"But why is the Wellbeing industry booming? Here are three key shifts driving the growth:"
""
"1.⁠ ⁠Silent Travel"
"Trips to the Slovenian Alps, Lake Tekapo in New Zealand and the High Atlas Mountains in Morocco have all become popular as of late. Travelers are increasingly drawn to remote, quiet landscapes that offer mental stillness and digital disconnection."
""
"2.⁠ ⁠Active Wellness"
"According to ABTA, 1 in 8 travellers booked an adventure holiday in the past year, rising to nearly 1 in 3 for 18-24s. Hikes and yoga retreats are becoming the new luxury."

Copenhagen just launched one of the smartest responses to overtourism I’ve seen."
""
"A tourism strategy that rewards contribution over consumption, and it’s working."
""
"Tourists in Copenhagen can help maintain a community garden in return for a freshly made lunch."
""
"Or even earn a free kayak rental just by collecting rubbish along the way."
""
"It’s all part of CopenPay, an initiative from Rikke Holm Petersen and the team at Wonderful Copenhagen that might be one of the most progressive tourism strategies I’ve seen in years."
""
"At a time when cities like Venice and Barcelona are overwhelmed by overtourism, and I’ve shared my strong opposition to visitor taxes, Copenhagen is offering a new model: Contribution-based tourism."
""
"The idea is to shift the visitor's mindset from passive consumer to active participant."
""
"The data proves it’s having an impact, with Copenhagen projecting 24% tourism growth by 2030. "
""
"For travel marketers, does this represent a credible pillar in your destination positioning? Should you be designing campaigns around value exchange rather than value extraction?"
""
"If it helps redistribute tourist flows and reduce pressure on overburdened places, I think the answer is fairly obvious."
""
"I’d love to hear from any tourism marketers that are doing this or have examples where this is being done, so we can share it on Beautiful Destinations!"
""
"Image Credit: Adrienne Murray
posts.hook: Copenhagen just launched one of the smartest responses to overtourism I’ve seen."

""

""
"1. Price and convenience still win. "
"Even loyal customers will switch if the alternative is cheaper or easier. "
""
"2. Loyalty programs lack personalization."
"They can’t compete with the way social media content inspires travellers with hyper-relevant, real-time ideas."
""
"3. Generational shifts."
"This is the most important one for me - younger travellers are less swayed by traditional programs, and more persuaded by the inspiration they see on social media and want to recreate for themselves. They favour unique experiences that they can do and share, over free breakfasts or wifi upgrades."
""
"But here's the interesting part:"
"By the end of 2025, the travel social media market will be worth $120 billion... 4x larger than the loyalty program market. That tells you everything."
""
"Could the real consumer loyalty engine today be investing in content, community and unique experiences for your guests that will make them want to keep coming back? For the next generation of traveler, I think so."
""
"📸 Lunch with Rafat Ali, CEO of Skift, discussing the future of travel, earlier this year!

posts.full_text:
If you produce world-class content, the algorithms will help you find your audience."
""
"It’s such a simple concept but is often overlooked by today's travel marketers."
""
"The majority of platforms that you market on, make money through advertising. To be appealing to advertisers, they need to show their audiences spend more time on their platforms, viewing, sharing and engaging in content."
""
"These platforms don’t make content themselves, they rely on brands, creators and individuals to do that. The platforms provide the technology and user experience to ensure their audience sees the content they want… and can be served an increasing load of ads."
""
"It’s why creators or brands like BD can build multi-million follower audiences and generate millions of monthly views without spending any money on paid marketing. Our content resonates with people, the algorithms do the rest."
""
"There is no reason why you can’t do the same - no matter what your product is."
""
"Here’s what works for us:"
""
"1. Lead with emotional insight "
"What’s your aim with your piece of content? Is it to inspire, to educate, to surprise? That clarity should guide every frame, start and end with that."
""
"2. Build for each platform, natively"
"Too many brands overlook the nuances of a multi-channel strategy. A single edit won’t land the same on TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube. Your strategy should shift on each platform you use- varying in length, format, visual style, music and message."
""
"3. Consistency beats perfection"
"Publish good content consistently for the same audience. The algorithms personalize your target audience’s feed, so consistency is key for organic performance."
""
"4. Study your analytics obsessively"
"The platforms give you the direction to take your content where your audience wants. Obsess over your analytics - it’s what every good brand does today. Every piece of content generates data, double down on what’s landing, and pivot fast when it’s not."
""
"Nail your organic performance first, it’s the foundational layer of all your marketing.
posts.hook: If you produce world-class content, the algorithms will help you find your audience."

I've spent the last decade watching travel brands make the same expensive mistake."
""
"They hire influencers when they need creators."
""
"In many interviews, I’ve been asked what the difference is between the two. "
""
"Here’s how I see it:"
""
"Influencers → media channels."
""
"You can analyse them in the way you’d analyse publications years ago. Who is their audience? What’s their reach? Do they align with our brand positioning? Their value is distribution."
""
"Creators → individuals akin to production studios."
""
"One person is the end-to-end producer, director, graphic designer, sound designer, and post-production. You have all that value in one person. Their value is content creation and storytelling. The occasional unicorn can be both."
""
"When paired with the right briefs and given the correct support structures, creators have the ability to transform business objectives into compelling content that has business impact. They do the roles that traditional agencies need many people, much time and even more money to execute."
""
"To many travel marketers, the terms get used interchangeably. But the distinction couldn’t be more important."
""
"Beautiful Destinations uses creators to understand our partners business objectives and produce content to meet them. It’s how we scale production, reduce costs, and deliver campaigns that resonate globally."
""
"As travel marketing has shifted towards always on, high quality short video content and smart social media distribution, the distinction between creators vs influencers matters more than ever.
posts.hook: I've spent the last decade watching travel brands make the same expensive mistake."

posts.full_text:
Last week, I was in Jamaica. It’s been a few years since I visited and the momentum of the country is undeniable."
""
"Since the start of 2025, Jamaica has welcomed 2.3 million visitors, increasing tourism revenue and showing a strong recovery since the pandemic. "
""
"It’s easy to attribute this to the country’s natural beauty or cultural richness - we all love Bob Marley and Usain Bolt. "
""
"But what’s driving real, long-term growth is the country’s strategic tourism plan - focused investments via Visit Jamaica into marketing, partnerships and infrastructure, led by my long-time friends Donovan White, Director of Tourism at Visit Jamaica and Minister of Tourism, Hon. Edmund Bartlett."
""
"There are a few ways they are doing this:"
""
"1. A 90-minute Travel Promise"
""
"An improved road system around the country. This is part of a broader plan to make sure every visitor can reach a resort from an airport or seaport in under 90 minutes."
""
"2. Game-Changing Hotel Developments"
""
"Jamaica currently has the Caribbean’s tallest hotel in development, which will be located in Montego Bay. It will be 33 stories high and have 5,000 rooms, bringing a huge amount of economic impact to the region. This is on top of the flagship success it has built with Sandals."
""
"3. Investing in a Tourism Workforce"
""
"Jamaica is offering certification programs to students to create a generation of job-ready young professionals entering the industry of tourism in the country.  With tourism representing almost a third of GDP, growing a well-trained and passionate workforce in the sector is critical."
""
"This growth has been intentional. For a country like Jamaica that has succeeded at tourism for so long, to be able to continue to grow, is a testament to the systems, infrastructure, education and vision for the future that the leadership has set."
""
"Jamaica has all of those in motion. I’m looking forward to seeing the full impact on the statistics towards the end of the year!
posts.hook: Last week, I was in Jamaica. It’s been a few years since I visited and the momentum of the country is undeniable."

A couple of weeks ago at Meta HQ in Silicon Valley, I learned something that could fundamentally reshape the way trips are planned."
""
"Under Sanjay Bhatia's leadership, Meta is evolving Meta AI into a fully integrated travel planning ecosystem."
""
"Reels changed the way people discover destinations. Now, Meta AI is changing how we act on that inspiration, enabling collaborative planning across the suite of Meta’s messaging apps."
""
"Rather than searching on a web browser and sending links manually, travelers are able to discover a destination from a Reel, then instantly ask Meta AI:"
"“Where is this?”"
"“How do I book this?”"
"“Can you send this to WhatsApp so me and my friends can plan it?”"
""
"The connection between Instagram DMs and WhatsApp group chats turns travel planning into a shared experience, fully contained within Meta’s ecosystem."
""
"It moves us a huge step closer to the integrated “super app” experience we have seen be so successful in China and, when you consider Expedia Group reported the average traveler visits 277 web pages before booking a trip, the opportunity to reduce that friction is enormous."
""
"If inspiration, research, group discussion, and booking all happen inside one ecosystem, and Google now indexes written content from IG posts, the role of social platforms in travel becomes even more powerful.
posts.hook: A couple of weeks ago at Meta HQ in Silicon Valley, I learned something that could fundamentally reshape the way trips are planned."

""

posts.full_text:
I grew up reading business books of great companies and how they operated, thinking that one day I’d be running businesses with thousands of employees and a huge office. "
""
"How wrong I was."
""
"The pandemic rocked our business. Overnight, 100% of our revenue was at risk, and our clients and their employees were at risk. We had a huge Madison Avenue head office, filled with racks of servers, computers, cameras, lenses, drones and people. We worked side by side every day, leveraging relationships over technology to run our company."
""
"But in the span of a week, we changed everything. All employees went permanently remote, all infrastructure moved into the cloud, all equipment was given to our most trusted creators and I promised everyone that we’d find a way to keep our culture and build back better."
""
"Here are the 5 things we did that still drive our company today:"
""
"1.⁠ ⁠Take the time to understand how each of your employees likes to work."
"Some of our team want the freedom of freelance, some want to live for months in different countries, some have young kids so need daily flexibility and some want full-time stability. We embrace it all."
""
"2.⁠ ⁠Foster and incentivize a culture of group online learning."
"We have tripled down on AI at BD and our Slack channels are on fire with insights, lessons and practical applications that team members are learning and sharing."
""
"3.⁠ ⁠Hire for hunger and adaptability. "
"In interviews, I always ask how and what a person likes to learn in their free time. I want to know the podcasts they listen to, the influences that inspire them and candidly, how much they push themselves to be better with self-directed learning. If you’re a motivated self-starter who constantly learns and adapts, you’ll succeed at BD."
""
"4.⁠ ⁠Maintain a flat, accessible org structure where titles do not matter."
"If you need slides for your pitch deck, a post on our social channels, a call to an unhappy client, a chase of an unpaid invoice, a review of an employment contract or absolutely anything else that will move our business forward, I’ll do it. We’ll all do it. There is no job too small if it helps us grow."
""
"5.⁠ ⁠And finally, when you do get together, make it memorable."
"This year’s BD retreat was at Sir Richard Branson’s private island, Moskito. It took a lot of time & resources to make it happen but it was worth every penny."
""
"This approach has allowed us to hire world-class talent from across the world and build a high-performing, high-growth business. I’m confident it will continue to do so."
""
"📸 Will Allen

posts.full_text:
The answer to overtourism isn’t more tourism tax. "
""
"Just this year alone, we’ve seen taxes imposed to address overtourism:"
"- Catalonia is set to double its tourist tax in 2025."
"- Venice will continue its tourist tax for day-trippers, with a fee of €5 if booked in advance and €10 for last-minute bookings (within 4 days.)"
"- From July, Santorini and Mykonos introduced a cruise tax of €20 per passenger in peak holiday season."
""
"This is a short-term solution to a long-term problem. The answer to dealing with overtourism is in redistribution, not restriction. "
""
"Instead of increasing the tax in hotspots, the industry needs to introduce tax subsidies or incentives to bring tourists to lesser-known destinations."
""
"For this to happen, the public sector needs to work with the private sector and catch up to the speed of consumers using social media."
""
"Imagine a system where:"
"- Governments reduce or remove hotel bed tax in secondary cities"
"- Tourism boards collaborate with private partners to promote quieter regions or pool capital to have greater marketing budgets as a collective"
"- Tax credits for Hotels in emerging areas who could pass on these savings to travelers or reinvest in experiences that will boost repeat visits"
""
"I know this is a hugely difficult issue with many important stakeholders to consider but increasing taxes on anything never gets my vote."
""
"If you’re in the travel industry, what do you think the solution to overtourism is? I imagine we’ll all have different opinions and I know this isn’t a simple problem to fix. "
""
"My interest comes from trying to learn more about how we can help with the audience we have and our content creation skills. "
""
"We want to discover lesser-known destinations. We want to support the governments in those destinations to better market themselves and we want to work with the entrepreneurs who have ideas they want the world to see."
""
"As I’ve been posting more and more on LinkedIn, the response from travel & tourism professionals has been amazing, so please keep the ideas and feedback coming!
posts.hook: The answer to overtourism isn’t more tourism tax. "

posts.full_text:
I’ve always loved the idea of luck. "
""
"What makes a person lucky? How can I become luckier? "
""
"Luck has played a huge part in my entrepreneurial journey and I can assure you it’s played a bigger role than most founders want to admit."
""
"Years ago, I came across the concept of the 4 Types of Luck by Dr. James Austin. Looking back, each type has shaped my career in different ways."
""
"1.⁠ ⁠Blind Luck"
"Probably the one we hear about most, the kind we can’t explain. The kind that just happens. Blind luck for me was discovering Instagram early. BD would not exist without the platform so I’m forever grateful to Adam Mosseri and his team! Did I see how things were going to turn out the day we started posting - definitely not! That was blind luck."
""
"2.⁠ ⁠Luck from constant action"
"This is the luck I most relate to. The one I think anyone can increase. Simply put- it’s more shots on goal, more meetings in pursuit of a deal, more trips in pursuit of an adventure. By the time any of the influential people in the world of travel discovered BD, we’d been putting out hundreds of high-quality posts daily, consistently increasing our surface area for luck."
""
"3.⁠ ⁠Luck in preparation"
"This is the luck you gain by being ready when the opportunity arises. Answering your call, being in the right place at the right time with the right skills to take that opportunity. I first spoke with the leadership of Expedia 10 years ago, so a decade later when social commerce became the phenomenon it has and Expedia presented the opportunity…we were ready to act."
""
"4.⁠ ⁠Luck that is unique to you"
"This is the luck you earn by being who you are. That unique balance we all have of life experiences, competence, ambition and timing coming together in a way that only you can grasp."
""
"For me, this defines my journey at BD. I loved to travel, I loved technology, I loved content and I loved business. To build a company doing exactly this has to be the luckiest thing that could have happened to me."
""
"You can’t manufacture luck but you can increase the likelihood that luck will find you by understanding the different types and making sure you show up :)"
""
"📸 Image with Adam Mosseri, Instagram's CEO last year, after a great conversation about social media, business and travel!
posts.hook: I’ve always loved the idea of luck. "

I've just left Google's offices with a realization that changes everything for travel brands."

"Google is now indexing content from Instagram Professional accounts, so posts can show up directly in Google searches. It’s the moment social media and search have finally merged."

"Think about what this means:"
"Your Instagram reel of a sunset in Santorini can now appear when someone searches "Places to visit in Greece" because you've paired it with an informative caption. Google has basically made educational storytelling the new search engine optimization."
""
"Combine this with building your AI “SEO” (how you show up in ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc) and…. 🤯🤯🤯"
""
"The leading travel brands in 2025 will be the ones creating scroll-stopping value-led content, not the ones with their old paid strategy in place."
""
"My advice would be to prioritise being discoverable in-platform first with world-class storytelling and value-led captions and combining that with a good understanding of how you show up in AI search."
""
"I'll have more to share from today's meeting at Google soon! 😉

In the early years of Beautiful Destinations, we left $100,000s on the table for what were considered quick, easy wins."

"We made a difficult, but thoughtful decision: We were going to sacrifice short-term cash, build our brand and credibility in travel, not be an influencer account."

"We declined all paid posts. "

"Instead, we focused on becoming excellent at content creation & growth, with a vision to shape travel culture and how people discover the world."

""
"50 million people and countless governments, hotels and airlines trust us because we’ve always led with world class content and a strong commitment to our brand."
""
"That’s something you can’t put a price on in my opinion.

China is teaching Western brands the secret to travel content: show your audience, don’t tell them."
""
"In China, they’re booking trips directly from the videos they watch. "
""
"When people are planning their next venture, they don’t open a search engine. They open Little Red Book, Xiaohongshu. "
""
"If you haven’t heard of it, it’s a social platform that’s a cross between Instagram, Pinterest, and Amazon, and is one of the most influential apps in China when it comes to consumer travel behavior."
""
"Audiences scroll, save and imagine themselves in the places they’re discovering. It’s a completely emotional, visual and experience-led journey. "
""
"Brands are building their content like creators, not institutions. And it’s why platforms like Xiaohongshu are reshaping how the next generation of travellers make decisions, long before they ever look at a booking site. "
""
"Meanwhile, in the West, a lot of brands are still publishing like it's 2013, focusing on static ads, stock content and campaigns built around conversions, not culture. "
""
"They’re leading with messaging, rarely focusing on experience and using platforms to sell when really they should be using them to give audiences an insight into the world they experience when they travel."
""
"But what I’ve learned is that travel content isn’t about volume anymore. It’s about resonance. Travellers, and especially younger travellers, are looking for identity and relatability. They want to feel seen and want content that isn’t an ad."
""
"And that’s what China’s travel content is getting right. It shows rather than tells. Western travel brands need to stop seeing TikTok and Reels as purely distribution channels and treat them as inspiration-booking engines instead. "
""
"That’s how the next generation is planning to travel and it’s the only long-term way you’re going to get them to book with you.
posts.hook: China is teaching Western brands the secret to travel content: show your audience, don’t tell them."

The moment His Highness, Sheikh Hamdan, Crown Prince of Dubai followed Beautiful Destinations, everything changed."
""
"Back then, I had no business plan for BD, no customers and no idea what social media could become. We were just sharing beautiful travel content on Instagram, which by chance caught the eye of His Highness."
""
"At that time, global leaders were not thinking about social media as a tool to grow their nation's brand or tourism industry. At best it was seen as something for fun, at worst a distraction not worth investing in. But Sheikh Hamdan saw it differently."
""
"He started following Beautiful Destinations, liking and sharing our content. "
""
"It put us on the radar of the leadership in Dubai, and shortly after the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism reached out to explore working together. We launched the world’s first Tourism Instameet hosting an event at the Royal Suite of the Burj Al Arab. Business Insider picked it up - check out the snarky headline, which was typical of social media coverage at the time :)"
""
"Ten years later, those partnerships have grown and grown. In January we launched Jumeirah’s global marketing campaign and in April the Beautiful Destinations Academy. We moved our business here, invested in more people & relationships and my wife and I have made Dubai our home."
""
"The biggest lesson I’d share with anyone who wants to succeed in business is to always play the long game. Good relationships, like good investments, compound. There’s a reason Einstein called compounding the 8th wonder of the world - it gets bigger, and more valuable over time, as should your business if you think long term."
""
"So much of the social media industry does not. Sheikh Hamdan saw the potential before most of the world did and the people who were my first partners in Dubai 10 years ago, are still leading tourism today :) Issam Kazim  Aida Al Busaidy
posts.hook: The moment His Highness, Sheikh Hamdan, Crown Prince of Dubai followed Beautiful Destinations, everything changed."

The more I’ve spoken at events around the world, the more I’ve learned that the same story can be told in a hundred different ways."
""
"But it only really lands when you understand the culture of the place you are in."
""
"The way you show up on stage, in a pitch, or in a boardroom needs to adapt to the people sitting in front of you. Without wanting to generalise too much, here are some cultural nuances I’ve learned…"
""
"🇺🇸 In the US, audiences usually love energy and a big personality."
"They definitely respond to big confidence, fast-paced delivery, and a pitch that is slick and sells."
""
"🌏 In a lot of Asia, it’s the opposite."
"The room values thoughtfulness & humility. Presenting is slower, more respectful, and more considered. Whenever I’m presenting in Asia, I always slow it right down."
""
"🌏 In areas of the Middle East, vision matters."
"You need to meet the scale of the room’s thinking if you want to get attention, with massive ambition and even bigger numbers. "
""
"🇧🇷 In Brazil, presentations are typically deeply emotional and more patriotic."
"I was over in Rio a couple of months ago to launch Beautiful Destinations' partnership with EMBRATUR - Brazilian Tourist Board and was fortunate to catch a couple of talks before me. Over there, it’s all about how people feel about their country and how your idea connects to that."
""
"When you’re doing business all across the world, I think understanding these nuances is what shows everyone that you’ve taken the time to understand who you’re speaking to and, fundamentally, that you’re invested in helping them win."
""
"Again - I’m not intending to make sweeping assumptions about countries and of course, there are anomalies to this, but I’m hoping to share how much more successful you can be in business if you take the time to learn, and respect different cultures.
posts.hook: The more I’ve spoken at events around the world, the more I’ve learned that the same story can be told in a hundred different ways."

posts.full_text:
The Digital Markets Act was built to make Europe’s digital economy fairer but right now, it’s under threat."
""
"A potential U.S. and EU trade deal could weaken the DMA by giving American tech giants, like Google, a say in how it’s enforced."
""
"Travel leaders like GetYourGuide and HomeToGo are pushing back, and they’re right to."
""
"As Johannes Reck, CEO of GetYourGuide, put it: "We either build a truly competitive digital market in Europe or we resign ourselves to becoming a digital backwater. I know which future I'm fighting for.""
""
"Whoever controls the platforms, controls how we discover travel and this will shape what destinations rise, what stories are told, and essentially where consumers travel to."
""
"For two decades, Google's search monopoly has shaped travel behavior. Today, it happens on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, and AI platforms… places where video drives decision-making."
""
"The DMA was introduced in 2022 and it represents the chance to break platform dominance and create space for innovation in travel discovery. That innovation in how people discover and experience travel is what the industry needs to meet the expectations of modern travelers."
""
"Consumers don’t want to follow the same paths they’ve been shown for the last two decades. They’re discovering through video. They’re searching in social. They want richer, faster, more connected experiences."
""
"If the DMA gets weakened, we risk locking travel discovery inside the same old platforms, just as social and AI are finally starting to shift power back to creators, communities, and destinations themselves."
""
"I don’t think we can have a future where discovery is dominated by only a handful of global players, do you?
posts.hook: The Digital Markets Act was built to make Europe’s digital economy fairer but right now, it’s under threat."

""
"The campaign's approach is brilliant: using the social platforms that created this imbalance to solve it."

"By launching videos on Instagram and TikTok from overcrowded hotspots like Venice and Florence, they're meeting travelers where they already discover destinations."
""
"For tourism boards worldwide, Visit Italy's strategy is a blueprint for over-tourism issues: embrace social media not just to promote, but to redistribute."
""
"When platforms naturally concentrate demand on viral destinations, smart destinations use those same platforms to consciously redirect it."
""
"This is something we’ve been doing at Beautiful Destinations, working with tourism boards to build strategies that manage traveler flows to highlight local communities."
""
"Destinations need to realise social media can be a flow management system 🇮🇹"
""
"Whilst the ENIT - Italian National Tourist Board is a separate entity governed by the Ministry of Tourism & Finance, their work to promote tourism to Italy has also been fantastic and this year they will be hosting the WTTC Global Summit in Rome."

"I can’t wait to come back to Italy!

""
"But here's what most people are missing:"
""
"Locals aren't just angry at travelers, they're angry at a broken system that funnels millions of people to the same handful of destinations."
""
"This is exactly the challenge social media was supposed to solve for travel marketing, yet we've made it worse."
""
"Instagram and TikTok algorithms have amplified the same viral hotspots, driving even more crowds to already saturated places like Barcelona's Park Güell or Rome's Trevi Fountain."
""
"The solution isn't fewer travelers, it's smarter distribution."
""
"There’s such a great opportunity here for travel brands and destinations to use content to showcase lesser-known regions that actually want and need tourism revenue."
""
"This is exactly what we aim to do at Beautiful Destinations. Over the years, we have used content to show lesser-known destinations like Albania, Kazakhstan, the Philippines and Montenegro because we know how social media can raise awareness in ways traditional media cannot."
""
"The future of sustainable tourism lies in using the right content on the right platforms to guide travellers to new places that will benefit from their presence."
""
"These locals are right, we have to do better - it’s in everyone’s interest.
posts.hook: The biggest coordinated anti-tourism protests in history just happened across Spain, Italy, and Portugal last weekend."

Ghana is positioning itself to become West Africa's tourism powerhouse and it's using a playbook that every destination should study 🌍"
""
"Yesterday, I met with Ghana's President, His Excellency John Dramani Mahama, and witnessed something amazing: the leadership of a country building its tourism future on authentic content rather than manufactured luxury."
""
"While East Africa has dominated tourism headlines, West Africa is quietly preparing its own tourism revolution. Ghana isn't trying to compete with Kenya's safari experiences or South Africa's wine regions."
""
"Instead, they're doing something smarter. "
""
"They're building on the success of their "Year of Return" campaign which brought hundreds of thousands of diaspora visitors home in 2019 and scaling it through sports, culture, and social media."
""
"The President's son, Sharaf Mahama, gets it. He understands that modern tourism isn't about billboards or brochures. It's about creating content that moves people on social channels. He invited me and former unified world heavy weight champion, Anthony Joshua, to visit Accra, experience a fantastic night of African boxing and meet with his father to discuss how we could increase tourism to Ghana."
""
"Watching AJ connect with local communities, seeing government officials, discussing Instagram strategies, and experiencing Accra for the first time reminded me why I love exploring new countries."
""
"Ghana is writing a playbook on how emerging destinations can use authentic cultural narratives to compete with established tourism giants and leverage social media to push their message to the world.
posts.hook: Ghana is positioning itself to become West Africa's tourism powerhouse and it's using a playbook that every destination should study 🌍"

posts.full_text:
We grew to 25 million Instagram followers in 10 years, let me tell you how…"
""
"When we launched Beautiful Destinations, we didn’t really have a plan with it, we just wanted to explore the world and share all the cool places we had the privilege of visiting."
""
"Ten years later, we’ve built one of the largest and most engaged travel communities in the world. But we didn’t get here by accident."
""
"Quickly, we spotted the opportunity if we adopted the right strategies… here’s exactly what worked for us:"
""
"1.⁠ ⁠Curated, world-class content"
"We built our reputation on world-class visuals. This carousel of the Bokty Mountain in West Kazakhstan gained 1,200,000 likes alone and grew our followers by thousands overnight."
""
"2.⁠ ⁠Strategic partnerships"
"We created early collaborations with global brands like Dubai Tourism and Marriott Hotels who wanted to explore social but didn’t know where to start. We delivered real business results and their leadership understood the value."
""
"3.⁠ ⁠Community over vanity"
"Every post is designed to spark curiosity and connection. This is a north star for us, we always ask ’Is there value from watching our content? Would you share it?’"
""
"4.⁠ ⁠Data-driven storytelling"
"Our edge has always been the ability to combine both data insights and storytelling. We tap into a global network of creators who can help us do this at scale."
""
"5.⁠ ⁠Evolving with the industry"
"We’ve evolved into many different services while staying true to the brand and values that got us here. We’re a driving force in how the travel industry views content."
""
"But 25 million followers alone does not build a business. You need to win clients, deliver value, recruit and retain great talent and build a reputation for quality and trust."
""
"We’re proud we can do that for destinations, brands, and governments today, helping them tell better stories and drive real-world results."
""
"Here’s to the next 25 million followers 😎
posts.hook: We grew to 25 million Instagram followers in 10 years, let me tell you how…"
